sentences.zh: 太宗十一子：孝莊文皇后生世祖，敏惠恭和元妃科爾沁博爾濟吉特氏生第八子，懿靖大貴妃阿巴海博爾濟吉特氏生襄親王博穆博果爾，元妃鈕祜祿氏生洛博會，繼妃烏喇納喇氏生肅親王豪格、洛格，側妃葉赫納喇氏生承澤親王碩塞，庶妃​​顏扎氏生輔國公葉布舒，庶妃納喇氏生鎮國公高塞，庶妃伊爾根覺羅氏生輔國公品級常舒，庶妃生輔國公韜塞。

translations.literal: Taizong had eleven sons: Empress Xiaozhuangwen bore the Shizu Emperor; the Primary Consort Minhuigonghe of the Khorchin Borjigit clan bore the eighth son; the Grand Consort Yijing of the Abahai Borjigit clan bore Prince Xiang Bomuboguo'er; the Primary Consort Niohuru bore Luobohui; the Successor Consort Ula Nara bore Prince Su Haoge and Luoge; the Secondary Consort Yehe Nara bore Chenze Prince Suose; the Common Consort Yanja bore Duke of the State Yebushu; the Common Consort Nara bore Prince of the State Gao Sai; the Common Consort Irgen Gioro bore Duke of the State at Rank Changshu; and a Common Consort bore Duke of the State Taosai.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had eleven sons. Empress Xiaozhuangwen bore the future Shizu Emperor. The primary consort Minhuigonghe of the Khorchin Borjigit clan bore an eighth son. The grand consort Yijing of the Abahai Borjigit clan bore Prince Xiang Bomuboguo'er. The primary consort Niohuru bore Luobohui. The successor consort Ula Nara bore Prince Su Haoge and Luoge. The secondary consort Yehe Nara bore Chenze Prince Suose. The common consort Yanja bore Duke of the State Yebushu; another common consort of the Nara clan bore Prince of the State Gao Sai; a common consort of the Irgen Gioro clan bore Duke of the State at Rank Changshu; and yet another common consort bore Duke of the State Taosai.

sentences.zh: 洛格、洛博會及第八子，皆殤，無封。

translations.literal: Luoge, Luobohui, and the eighth son all died young and received no titles.
translations.idiomatic: Luoge, Luobohui, and the eighth son all died in infancy and were never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 肅武親王豪格，太宗第一子。

translations.literal: Prince Suwu Haoge was Taizong's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Suwu Haoge was Emperor Taizong's firstborn son.

sentences.zh: 初從征蒙古董夔、察哈爾、鄂爾多斯諸部，有功，授貝勒。

translations.literal: At first he followed campaigns against the Mongol tribes of Dongkui, Chakhar, and Ordos, performed merit, and was appointed beile.
translations.idiomatic: He first took part in campaigns against the Dongkui, Chakhar, and Ordos Mongols, distinguished himself, and was made a beile.

sentences.zh: 天命十一年，偕貝勒代善等徵扎嚕特部，斬其貝勒鄂齋圖。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianming, together with Beile Daishan and others he campaigned against the Jarut tribe and beheaded their beile Ezhaitu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianming, he joined Beile Daishan and others in a campaign against the Jarut, killing their beile Ezhaitu.

sentences.zh: 天聰元年，敗明兵於錦州，。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiancong he defeated Ming troops at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiancong, he defeated Ming forces at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，偕？

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, together with Abatai and others
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year, he joined Abatai and others

sentences.zh: 塔山糧運。

translations.literal: he seized the grain transports at Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: he took the grain convoys at Tashan.

sentences.zh: 二年，偕濟爾哈朗討蒙古固特塔布囊，誅之，收其？

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Jirhalang he punished the Mongol Gutu tabunang, executed him, and took his followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, he and Jirhalang campaigned against the Mongol Gutu tabunang, put him to death, and absorbed his followers.

sentences.zh: 复率偏師貝勒莽古爾泰等視通州渡口，師薄明都，豪格迎擊寧、錦援兵於廣渠門外，敵伏於右，豪格以所部當之，衝擊至城壕，明兵大潰，偕岳託、薩哈璘圍永平，克香河。

translations.literal: Again leading a detached force with Beile Manggu'ertai and others he reconnoitered the Tongzhou crossing; when the army approached the Ming capital, Haoge met the Ning and Jin relief troops outside Guangqu Gate. The enemy lay in ambush on the right; Haoge met them with his own command, charged to the city moat, and the Ming army broke in great disorder. Together with Yuetuo and Sahalian he besieged Yongping and took Xianghe.
translations.idiomatic: He again led a detached column with Beile Manggu'ertai and others to scout the Tongzhou ford. As the main army neared the Ming capital, Haoge intercepted Ning–Jin relief troops outside Guangqu Gate. Enemy forces lay in ambush on the right; Haoge threw his own troops against them and drove the charge to the city moat until the Ming lines collapsed. He then joined Yuetuo and Sahalian in besieging Yongping and captured Xianghe.

sentences.zh: 六年，從伐察哈爾，移師入明邊，略歸化諸路。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against Chakhar, shifted the army into Ming territory, and raided the routes around Guihua.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he joined the campaign against Chakhar, then moved the army into Ming territory and raided the Guihua region.

sentences.zh: 六月，進和碩貝勒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he was advanced to Prince of the State (heshuo beile).
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was promoted to heshuo beile.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔問徵明與朝鮮、察哈爾三者何先，疏言：「徵明，如徒得錦州，餘堅壁不下及邊外新舊蒙古從舊道入，諭各屯寨，以我慾和而彼君不？

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict asked which should come first among campaigning against Ming, Korea, and Chakhar. He memorialized: 'In campaigning against Ming, if we only take Jinzhou while the rest hold their walls and do not submit, and if the old and new Mongols beyond the border enter by the old route to instruct each stockaded post that we desire peace while their ruler does not consent'
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the court asked whether war against Ming, Korea, or Chakhar should take priority. He replied in a memorial: 'Against Ming, if we capture only Jinzhou while other strongholds refuse to yield, and if Mongols old and new beyond the frontier enter by the old road to tell each fortified post that we seek peace while their sovereign will not consent'

sentences.zh: ，曠日持久，恐老我師。

translations.literal: , the affair will drag on day after day and we may wear out our army.
translations.idiomatic: , the campaign will drag on indefinitely and risk exhausting our troops.

sentences.zh: 宜悉我答，彼將自怨其主。

translations.literal: We should answer them fully; they will then blame their own ruler.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to answer them at length so that they will turn against their own sovereign.

sentences.zh: 再用更番法，俟馬肥，益以漢兵巨？

translations.literal: Then use rotation in relays, wait until the horses are fat, and add Han troops and heavy cannon
translations.idiomatic: Then employ relay rotations, wait until the horses are in condition, and reinforce with Han troops and heavy cannon

sentences.zh: ，一出寧遠，一出舊道，夾攻山海關，不得，則屯兵招諭流賊，駐師通州，待其懈而擊之。

translations.literal: ; one column out from Ningyuan and one by the old road to attack Shanhaiguan from both sides. If that fails, station troops to summon and persuade bandits, hold the army at Tongzhou, and strike when they slacken.
translations.idiomatic: ; one force from Ningyuan and one along the old route to take Shanhaiguan in a pincer. Failing that, encamp to win over roving bandits, hold the army at Tongzhou, and attack when the enemy relaxes.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮、察哈爾且緩圖焉。

translations.literal: Korea and Chakhar may be dealt with more slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Korea and Chakhar can wait for later planning.

sentences.zh: 」八月，略山海關。

translations.literal: ' In the eighth month he raided Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the eighth month he raided the Shanhaiguan region.

sentences.zh: 八年，從上自宣府趨朔州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he followed the emperor from Xuanfu toward Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he followed the emperor from Xuanfu toward Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 豪格偕揚古利毀邊牆，分兵自尚方堡入，略朔州及五台山，從上視大同，擊敗明援兵。

translations.literal: Haoge, together with Yangguli, destroyed the border wall and divided the army to enter from Shangfang Fort, raided Shuozhou and Wutai Mountain, followed the emperor in reconnoitering Datong, and defeated Ming relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Haoge and Yangguli breached the frontier wall, sent a detachment in through Shangfang Fort, raided Shuozhou and Mount Wutai, accompanied the emperor to inspect Datong, and routed Ming relief forces.

sentences.zh: 九年，偕多爾袞等收察哈爾林丹汗子額哲，抵托里圖，定盟。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, together with Dorgon and others, he received Chakhar Lind Khan's son Eje, reached Tuolitu, and fixed an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he joined Dorgon and others in receiving Lind Khan's son Eje of Chakhar, reached Tuolitu, and concluded an alliance.

sentences.zh: 還抵歸化城，复略山西邊郡，毀寧武關，入代州、忻州。

translations.literal: Returning to Guihua City, he again raided the border prefectures of Shanxi, destroyed Ningwu Pass, and entered Daizhou and Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the return to Guihua he raided Shanxi's frontier districts again, broke Ningwu Pass, and entered Daizhou and Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年四月，進封肅親王，掌戶部事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chongde he was advanced to Prince Su and placed in charge of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first Chongde year he was made Prince Su and given charge of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋坐黨岳託漏上言有怨心，降貝勒，解任，罰銀千。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for siding with Yuetuo in leaking a memorial that showed resentment, he was reduced to beile, removed from office, and fined one thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was demoted to beile, stripped of his post, and fined a thousand taels of silver for siding with Yuetuo in leaking a resentful memorial.

sentences.zh: 旋偕多爾袞攻錦州，仍攝戶部。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he joined Dorgon in attacking Jinzhou and again acted as head of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Dorgon in the attack on Jinzhou while continuing to oversee the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 又從征朝鮮，偕多爾袞別自寬甸入長山口，克昌州，敗安州、黃州兵於寧邊城下。

translations.literal: He also followed the campaign in Korea; with Dorgon he separately entered by Kuandian through Changshan Pass, took Changzhou, and defeated the troops of Anzhou and Huangzhou below Ningbian City.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the Korean campaign. He and Dorgon entered separately from Kuandian through Changshan Pass, captured Changzhou, and defeated Anzhou and Huangzhou forces below Ningbian.

sentences.zh: 復遣將敗其援兵，次宣屯村，村民言：「黃州守將聞國王被圍，遣兵萬五千往援，行三日矣。

translations.literal: He again sent generals to defeat their relief force. Halting at Xuantun Village, villagers said: 'The Huangzhou commander, hearing the king is besieged, has sent fifteen thousand troops in relief; they have been marching three days.'
translations.idiomatic: He sent officers again to defeat enemy reinforcements. At Xuantun Village the locals reported: 'The Huangzhou commander, learning the king is surrounded, has dispatched fifteen thousand men in relief—they have already marched three days.'

sentences.zh: 」我軍疾馳一晝夜，追及於陶山，擊敗之。

translations.literal: ' Our army raced day and night, overtook them at Taoshan, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: ' Our troops forced a day-and-night march, caught them at Taoshan, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 九月，坐固山額真鄂莫克圖欲脅取蒙古台吉博洛女媚事豪格，豪格不治其罪，罷部任，罰銀千。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Gushan ejen Emoketu had tried to seize the Mongol taiji Boluo's daughter to curry favor with Haoge and Haoge did not punish his crime, he was removed from the ministry post and fined one thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he lost his ministry post and was fined a thousand taels because Gushan ejen Emoketu had tried to force Boluo's daughter on Haoge as a bribe and Haoge had not punished him.

sentences.zh: 三年九月，伐明，自董家口毀邊牆入，敗明兵於豐潤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year he campaigned against Ming, entered by destroying the wall at Dongjiakou, and defeated Ming troops at Fengrun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the third year he invaded Ming territory through a breach at Dongjiakou and defeated Ming forces at Fengrun.

sentences.zh: 遂下山東，降高唐，略地至曹州，還下東光。

translations.literal: He then descended into Shandong, received the surrender of Gaotang, raided as far as Caozhou, and returned to take Dongguang.
translations.idiomatic: He then pushed into Shandong, accepted Gaotang's surrender, raided as far as Caozhou, and on the return captured Dongguang.

sentences.zh: 又遣騎二千破明兵，克獻縣。

translations.literal: He also sent two thousand horsemen to defeat Ming troops and take Xian County.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched two thousand cavalry, routed Ming troops, and captured Xian County.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，師還，賜馬二、銀萬，复攝戶部，復原封。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year the army returned; he was given two horses and ten thousand taels of silver, again placed over the Board of Revenue, and restored to his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned in the fourth month of the fourth year he received two horses and ten thousand taels of silver, resumed direction of the Board of Revenue, and was restored to his former title.

sentences.zh: 又偕多鐸敗寧遠兵，斬明將金國鳳。

translations.literal: Again with Duoduo he defeated Ningyuan troops and beheaded the Ming general Jin Guofeng.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Duoduo in defeating Ningyuan forces and killed the Ming general Jin Guofeng.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，偕多爾袞屯田義州，刈錦州禾，克台九、小凌河西台二。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, together with Dorgon he garrisoned and farmed at Yizhou, reaped the grain of Jinzhou, and took Platform Nine and the two platforms west of Xiaoling River.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifth year he and Dorgon encamped to farm at Yizhou, harvested Jinzhou grain, and captured Platform Nine and two western platforms on the Xiaoling River.

sentences.zh: 明兵夜出襲鑲藍旗營，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Ming troops came out at night to attack the Bordered Blue Banner camp and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ming forces made a night assault on the Bordered Blue Banner camp and were beaten off.

sentences.zh: 又擊洪承疇杏山，偕多爾袞圍錦州。

translations.literal: He again struck Hong Chengchou at Xingshan and with Dorgon besieged Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again engaged Hong Chengchou at Xingshan and joined Dorgon in besieging Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐離城遠駐，復遣兵還家，降郡王。

translations.literal: For encamping far from the city and again sending troops home, he was reduced to prince of the second degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prince of the second degree for keeping his camp too far from the city and again allowing troops to return home.

sentences.zh: 六年，再圍錦州，擊松山及山海關援兵，皆敗之，獲馬五百餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again besieged Jinzhou, struck relief from Songshan and Shanhaiguan, defeated them all, and captured more than five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he besieged Jinzhou again, defeated relief columns from Songshan and Shanhaiguan, and took more than five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 承疇將兵十三萬援錦州，破其壘三。

translations.literal: Chengchou led one hundred thirty thousand men to relieve Jinzhou; three of his camps were broken.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou marched one hundred thirty thousand troops to relieve Jinzhou; three of his encampments were overrun.

sentences.zh: 上至軍，將駐高橋，豪格等恐敵約軍夾攻，請改屯松山、杏山間。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached the army he intended to encamp at Gaoqiao; Haoge and others, fearing the enemy would coordinate armies for a pincer attack, asked to shift camp between Songshan and Xingshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor joined the army he planned to camp at Gaoqiao. Haoge and others, fearing a coordinated enemy pincer, asked to move the camp between Songshan and Xingshan instead.

sentences.zh: 七年，松山明將夏承德密遣人請降，以其子舒為質，豪格遣左右翼夜梯城入，八旗兵繼之，旦，克松山，獲承疇及巡撫邱民仰等，斬官百餘、兵千六十有奇。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Ming general Xia Chengde of Songshan secretly sent men to offer surrender, giving his son Shu as hostage. Haoge sent the left and right wings to scale the wall by night; the Eight Banners followed, and at dawn Songshan was taken. Chengchou and Grand Coordinator Qiu Minyang were captured; more than one hundred officers and somewhat over one thousand sixty soldiers were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Xia Chengde of Songshan secretly sent envoys to surrender, offering his son Shu as hostage. Haoge sent both wings to scale the walls at night; the Eight Banners followed, and by dawn Songshan had fallen. Chengchou and Grand Coordinator Qiu Minyang were taken; over one hundred officers and more than sixteen hundred soldiers were executed.

sentences.zh: 進駐杏山，复偕濟爾哈朗克塔山。

translations.literal: Advancing to encamp at Xingshan, he again joined Jirhalang in taking Tashan.
translations.idiomatic: He moved forward to Xingshan and again joined Jirhalang in capturing Tashan.

translations.literal: For his
translations.idiomatic: For his

sentences.zh: 功，復原封，賜鞍馬一、蟒緞百。

translations.literal: For merit he was restored to his original rank and given one saddled horse and one hundred bolts of python-patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was restored to his former rank and rewarded with a saddled horse and one hundred bolts of python brocade.

sentences.zh: 順治元年四月，以語​​侵睿親王多爾袞，為固山額真何洛會所訐，坐削爵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first Shunzhi year, for words that insulted Prince Rui Dorgon, he was impeached by gushan ejen Heluohui and deprived of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first Shunzhi year he lost his title after remarks insulting Prince Rui Dorgon were reported by gushan ejen Heluohui.

sentences.zh: 十月，大封諸王，念豪格從定中原有功，仍復原封。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, when princes were enfeoffed on a grand scale, remembering Haoge's merit in pacifying the Central Plains, his original rank was again restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, during the great enfeoffment of princes, Haoge was restored to his former rank in recognition of his service in pacifying the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，定濟寧滿家洞土寇，堙山洞二百五十一。

translations.literal: That winter he pacified the bandits of Manjiadong in Jining and filled in two hundred fifty-one mountain caves.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he suppressed the Manjiadong bandits in Jining and sealed two hundred fifty-one mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 三年，命為靖遠大將軍，偕衍禧郡王羅洛渾、貝勒尼堪等西征。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand General Jingyuan and, together with Prince of the Second Degree Yanxi Luolohun, Beile Nikan, and others, marched west.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was named Grand General Jingyuan and marched west with Prince Yanxi Luolohun, Beile Nikan, and others.

sentences.zh: 師次西安，遣尚書星訥等破敵邠州，別遣固山額真都類攻慶陽。

translations.literal: The army halted at Xi'an; he sent Minister Xingne and others to defeat the enemy at Binzhou and separately dispatched gushan ejen Dulei to attack Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The army stopped at Xi'an. He sent Minister Xingne and others to rout the enemy at Binzhou and dispatched gushan ejen Dulei separately against Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 時賀珍、二隻虎、孫守法據漢中、興安，武大定、高如礪、蔣登雷、石國璽、王可成、周克德據徽縣、階州。

translations.literal: At the time He Zhen, Erzhihu, and Sun Shoufa held Hanzhong and Xing'an; Wu Dading, Gao Ruli, Jiang Denglei, Shi Guoxi, Wang Kecheng, and Zhou Kede held Huixian and Jiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhen, Erzhihu, and Sun Shoufa then held Hanzhong and Xing'an; Wu Dading, Gao Ruli, Jiang Denglei, Shi Guoxi, Wang Kecheng, and Zhou Kede held Huixian and Jiezhou.

sentences.zh: 師自西安分兵進擊，登雷、國璽、可成、克德俱降，餘潰走，下所陷城邑。

translations.literal: The army divided forces from Xi'an to advance; Denglei, Guoxi, Kecheng, and Kede all surrendered, the rest broke and fled, and the cities they had seized were taken.
translations.idiomatic: From Xi'an the army advanced in columns. Denglei, Guoxi, Kecheng, and Kede all submitted; the rest scattered, and the towns they had occupied were recovered.

sentences.zh: 陝西平。

translations.literal: Shaanxi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十一月，入四川，張獻忠據西充，遣巴牙喇昂邦鰲拜先發，師繼進，抵西充，大破之，豪格親射獻忠，殪，平其壘百三十餘所，斬首數万級。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he entered Sichuan. Zhang Xianzhong held Xichong; he sent the banner officer Oboi ahead, the army followed, reached Xichong, and won a great victory. Haoge himself shot Xianzhong and killed him, leveled more than one hundred thirty of his stockades, and beheaded tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he entered Sichuan. Zhang Xianzhong was at Xichong; Haoge sent banner officer Oboi ahead, then followed with the main force, routed the rebels at Xichong, and personally shot Xianzhong dead. He destroyed more than one hundred thirty rebel strongholds and took tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，上嘉？

translations.literal: When news of victory arrived, the emperor commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When victory was reported, the emperor commended him.

translations.literal: Him.
translations.idiomatic: him.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，遵義、夔州、茂州、榮昌、隆昌、富順、內江、寶陽諸郡縣悉定。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year the prefectures and counties of Zunyi, Kuizhou, Maozhou, Rongchang, Longchang, Fushun, Neijiang, Baoyang, and others were all secured.
translations.idiomatic: By the eighth month of the fourth year Zunyi, Kuizhou, Maozhou, Rongchang, Longchang, Fushun, Neijiang, Baoyang, and the other districts had all been secured.

sentences.zh: 四川平。

translations.literal: Sichuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，師還，上御太和殿宴勞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year the army returned; the emperor held a feast of reward at the Hall of Supreme Harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned in the second month of the fifth year, the emperor feasted the troops at the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 睿親王多爾袞與豪格有夙隙，坐豪格徇隱部將冒功及擢用罪人揚善弟吉賽，系豪格於獄。

translations.literal: Prince Rui Dorgon and Haoge had an old feud; on the grounds that Haoge shielded a subordinate who falsely claimed merit and promoted Jisai, brother of the criminal Yang Shan, Haoge was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui Dorgon and Haoge had long been at odds. Haoge was jailed for covering up a subordinate's false claims of merit and for promoting Jisai, brother of the condemned Yang Shan.

sentences.zh: 三月，薨。

translations.literal: In the third month he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month.

sentences.zh: 睿親王納豪格福晉，嘗召其子富綬至邸校射。

translations.literal: Prince Rui took Haoge's primary consort and once summoned his son Fushou to the residence for archery practice.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rui took Haoge's principal consort and once summoned his son Fushou to his mansion for archery.

sentences.zh: 何洛會語人曰：「見此鬼魅，令人心悸，何不除之？

translations.literal: Heluohui said to others: 'Seeing this ghostly creature makes one's heart tremble—why not remove him?'
translations.idiomatic: Heluohui told others, 'That ghost of a boy sets the heart pounding—why not do away with him?'

sentences.zh: 」錫翰以告，睿親王曰：「何洛會意，因爾不知我愛彼也。

translations.literal: ' Xihan reported this; Prince Rui said: 'That is Heluohui's meaning, because you do not know that I love the boy.'
translations.idiomatic: ' Xihan reported it. Prince Rui said, 'That is Heluohui's view—you do not realize how fond I am of the boy.'

sentences.zh: 」由是得全。

translations.literal: ' Thus he was preserved unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: ' In this way the boy was spared.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，上親政，雪豪格枉，复封和碩肅親王，立碑表之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the emperor took personal rule, cleared Haoge's injustice, again enfeoffed him as Prince Su of the first rank, and erected a stele in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year, when the emperor assumed personal rule, he cleared Haoge's wrongful treatment, restored him posthumously as Prince Su of the first rank, and set up a commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 十三年，追諡。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year a posthumous title was granted.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous title was conferred in the thirteenth year.

sentences.zh: 親王得諡自豪格始。

translations.literal: Princes receiving posthumous titles began with Haoge.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of granting posthumous titles to princes of the first rank began with Haoge.

sentences.zh: 以諡系封號上，曰武肅親王。

translations.literal: The posthumous name was placed before the title, making him Prince Suwu.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous epithet was prefixed to his title, yielding Prince Suwu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十三年，配享太廟。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Qianlong he was given joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third Qianlong year he was granted joint worship in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 豪格子七，有爵者二：富綬、猛瓘。

translations.literal: Haoge had seven sons; two held titles: Fushou and Mengguan.
translations.idiomatic: Haoge had seven sons, of whom two held noble ranks: Fushou and Mengguan.

sentences.zh: 富綬襲爵，改號曰顯親王。

translations.literal: Fushou inherited the title, which was changed to Prince Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Fushou inherited the title, which was then changed to Prince Xian.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，薨，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he died; his posthumous title was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth Kangxi year and was posthumously titled Yi.

sentences.zh: 子丹臻，襲。

translations.literal: His son Danzhen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Danzhen succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從征噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the campaign against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he took part in the campaign against Galdan.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，薨，諡曰密。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he died; his posthumous title was Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-first year and was posthumously titled Mi.

sentences.zh: 子衍潢，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yanhuang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanhuang succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，薨，年八十二，諡曰謹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong he died at age eighty-two; his posthumous title was Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-sixth Qianlong year at eighty-two and was posthumously titled Jin.

sentences.zh: 富綬孫蘊著，襲。

translations.literal: Fushou's grandson Yunzhu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Fushou's grandson Yunzhu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，自三等輔國將軍授內閣侍讀學士，歷通政使、盛京戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Qianlong, from third-rank aide-de-camp general of the state he was appointed Reader in the Grand Secretariat, then served as Commissioner of the Transmission Office and Vice Minister of Revenue at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he rose from third-rank aide-de-camp general of the state to Reader in the Grand Secretariat, then served as Transmission Commissioner and Vice Minister of Revenue at Mukden.

sentences.zh: 調兵部侍郎，遷漕運總督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of War and promoted to Governor-General of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Vice Minister of War and then appointed Governor-General of the Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 坐受商人餽遺，謬稱上旨籍鹽政吉慶家，坐絞，上寬之，复授副都統，歷涼州、綏遠城將軍，工部尚書。

translations.literal: For accepting gifts from merchants and falsely claiming an imperial order to confiscate the household of Salt Controller Jiqing, he was sentenced to strangulation; the emperor showed mercy, again appointed him vice commander-in-chief, and he served as garrison general at Liangzhou and Suiyuan and as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was condemned to strangulation for taking merchants' gifts and falsely claiming an imperial order to confiscate Salt Controller Jiqing's property. The emperor pardoned him, reappointed him vice commander-in-chief, and he later served as garrison general at Liangzhou and Suiyuan and as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 既，襲封。

translations.literal: Afterward he inherited the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded to the princely title.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，复號肅親王。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year the title Prince Su was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year the house was again styled Prince Su.

sentences.zh: 薨，年八十，諡曰勤。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty; his posthumous title was Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously titled Qin.

sentences.zh: 丹臻孫永錫，襲。

translations.literal: Danzhen's grandson Yongxi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Danzhen's grandson Yongxi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 官都統。

translations.literal: He held the post of commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He served as commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 坐事，罷。

translations.literal: For an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，薨，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he died; his posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first Daoguang year and was posthumously titled Gong.

sentences.zh: 子敬敏，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jingmin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingmin succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, he died; his posthumous title was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Xianfeng year he died and was posthumously titled Shen.

sentences.zh: 子華豐，襲，歷內大臣、宗令。

translations.literal: His son Huafeng succeeded and served as Grand Minister of the Interior and Head of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huafeng succeeded to the title and held the posts of Grand Minister of the Interior and Head of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 以火器營設碓製藥，佔用王府地，華豐力拒之，詔責不知大體，罷宗令、內大臣。

translations.literal: Because the Firearms Brigade set up a pestle-mill to manufacture medicine and occupied princely estate land, Huafeng vigorously resisted; an edict rebuked him for failing to grasp the larger situation and removed him from his posts as Head of the Imperial Clan Court and Grand Minister of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: When the Firearms Brigade installed a mortar to make medicines on princely land, Huafeng resisted forcefully. The court rebuked him for lacking a sense of the larger situation and dismissed him as Head of the Imperial Clan Court and Grand Minister of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 八年，薨，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he died; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died and was posthumously titled Ke.

sentences.zh: 子隆懃，襲，官內大臣。

translations.literal: His son Longqin succeeded and held the office of Grand Minister of the Interior.
translations.idiomatic: His son Longqin succeeded and served as Grand Minister of the Interior.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十一年，疏請納正言、裕財用，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Guangxu, he memorialized requesting that upright counsel be heeded and state revenues be strengthened; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first Guangxu year he submitted a memorial urging the court to heed honest counsel and strengthen the treasury; the emperor commended and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，薨，諡曰良。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he died; his posthumous title was Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he died and was posthumously titled Liang.

sentences.zh: 子善耆，襲。

translations.literal: His son Shanqi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanqi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，授民政部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, he was appointed Minister of Civil Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was appointed Minister of Civil Affairs.

sentences.zh: 遜國後，避居大連灣。

translations.literal: After the abdication of the dynasty, he lived in seclusion at Dalian Bay.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynasty's abdication he withdrew to live at Dalian Bay.

sentences.zh: 久之，薨，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: After a long while, he died; his posthumous title was Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Many years later he died and was posthumously titled Zhong.

sentences.zh: 溫良郡王猛瓘，豪格第五子。

translations.literal: Prince of the Commandery of Wenliang, Meng'an, was the fifth son of Haoge.
translations.idiomatic: Meng'an, Prince of the Commandery of Wenliang, was Haoge's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 順治十四年，封。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Shunzhi, he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth Shunzhi year he received his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，薨。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth Kangxi year he died.

sentences.zh: 子佛永惠，襲。

translations.literal: His son Foyonghui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Foyonghui succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，降貝勒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, he was demoted to beile.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was reduced to beile.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子揆惠，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: His son Kuihui succeeded to the title of Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuihui succeeded as Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: For an offense, his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his title for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 延信，猛瓘第三子。

translations.literal: Yanxin was the third son of Meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxin was Meng'an's third son.

sentences.zh: 初封奉國將軍。

translations.literal: He was initially enfeoffed as General Who Supports the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as General Who Supports the State.

sentences.zh: 累官至都統。

translations.literal: He rose through successive offices to Banner General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Banner General.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，從撫遠大將軍貝子允率師討策妄阿喇布坦，駐西寧。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, he followed the Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief, Prince Yin'e, leading troops to campaign against Tsewang Araptan, and was stationed at Xining.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year he served under the Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief, Prince Yin'e, campaigning against Tsewang Araptan and encamping at Xining.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，授平逆將軍，率師徇西藏，道青海，擊敗策妄阿喇布坦將策零敦多卜，遂入西藏。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, he was appointed General Who Pacifies Rebels, led troops toward Tibet by way of Qinghai, defeated Tsewang Araptan's general Tsering Donrub, and then entered Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year he was made General Who Pacifies Rebels, marched on Tibet through Qinghai, routed Tsewang Araptan's general Tsering Donrub, and entered Tibet.

sentences.zh: 西藏平。

translations.literal: Tibet was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「平逆將軍延信領滿洲、蒙古、綠旗各軍，經自古未闢之道，煙瘴惡溪，人跡罕見。

translations.literal: The edict said: 'General Who Pacifies Rebels Yanxin led the Manchu, Mongol, and Green Standard armies along routes never opened since antiquity, through malarial vapors and treacherous streams where human tracks were rarely seen.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: 'General Who Pacifies Rebels Yanxin commanded Manchu, Mongol, and Green Standard forces along paths never traveled since antiquity, through miasmic gorges and poisonous streams where few had ever passed.

sentences.zh: 身臨絕域，殲夷醜類，勇略可嘉！

translations.literal: He went in person to the farthest regions, destroyed the vile enemy, and his courage and strategy are worthy of praise!'
translations.idiomatic: He entered the uttermost frontier in person, destroyed the wicked foe, and his courage and strategy deserve praise!'

sentences.zh: 封輔國公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 」尋攝撫遠大將軍事。

translations.literal: ' Soon afterward he acted as Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: ' Soon after he served as acting Pacification Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 揆惠既奪爵，議以延信襲。

translations.literal: Since Kuihui had had his title stripped, it was proposed that Yanxin should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After Kuihui was stripped of his title, the court proposed that Yanxin inherit.

sentences.zh: 進貝子，再進貝勒。

translations.literal: He was promoted to beizi, then promoted again to beile.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to beizi and then again to beile.

sentences.zh: 授西安將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，上以延信與阿其那等結黨，又陰結允，徇年羹堯，入藏侵帑十萬兩，奪爵，逮下王大臣按治。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, the emperor concluded that Yanxin had formed a faction with Aqina and others, had also secretly joined Yin'e, indulged Nian Gengyao, and upon entering Tibet embezzled one hundred thousand taels from the treasury; his title was stripped and he was handed over to princes and ministers for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth Yongzheng year the emperor found that Yanxin had banded with Aqina and others, secretly colluded with Yin'e, catered to Nian Gengyao, and embezzled one hundred thousand taels upon entering Tibet. His title was taken and he was handed to princes and ministers for trial.

sentences.zh: 讞上延信黨援、欺罔、負恩、要結人心、貪婪亂政、失誤兵機，凡二十罪，當斬，上命幽禁，子孫降紅帶。

translations.literal: The verdict listed Yanxin's crimes of factional support, deception, ingratitude, currying popular favor, greedy and disorderly governance, and failure in military timing—twenty crimes in all—and sentenced him to decapitation; the emperor ordered him imprisoned instead, and his descendants were demoted to red belts.
translations.idiomatic: The finding charged Yanxin with twenty offenses, including factional backing, deceit, ingratitude, winning hearts for himself, greedy misrule, and military blunders, and called for decapitation. The emperor ordered imprisonment instead, and his descendants were reduced to red belts.

sentences.zh: 輔國公葉布舒，太宗第四子。

translations.literal: Duke Who Assists the State Yepushu was the fourth son of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Yepushu, Duke Who Assists the State, was Taizong's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 初封鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: He was initially enfeoffed as General Who Guards the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first enfeoffed as General Who Guards the State.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，晉輔國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, he was promoted to Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Kangxi year he was promoted to Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he died.

sentences.zh: 子蘇爾登，降襲鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: His son Su'erdeng succeeded at reduced rank as General Who Guards the State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su'erdeng inherited at reduced rank as General Who Guards the State.

sentences.zh: 承澤裕親王碩塞，太宗第五子。

translations.literal: Chenze Prince Su of the First Rank, Shuosai, was the fifth son of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shuosai, Chenze Prince Su of the First Rank, was Taizong's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，封。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi, he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Shunzhi year he received his enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 時李自成奔潼關，河以南仍為自成守。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zicheng fled to Tong Pass, and south of the Yellow River the territory was still held by Zicheng's forces.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Zicheng fled toward Tong Pass, while lands south of the Yellow River remained in Zicheng's hands.

sentences.zh: 碩塞從豫親王多鐸師次孟津，進攻陝州，破自成將張有增、劉方亮，自成迎戰，又大破之。

translations.literal: Shuosai followed Prince Yu Duo Duo, whose army encamped at Mengjin, advanced to attack Shaanzhou, defeated Zicheng's generals Zhang Youzeng and Liu Fangliang, and when Zicheng came out to fight was again heavily defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Shuosai followed Prince Yu Duo Duo to camp at Mengjin and attack Shaanzhou, routing Zicheng's generals Zhang Youzeng and Liu Fangliang; when Zicheng came out to meet them, he was routed again.

sentences.zh: 師入關，斬其將馬世堯。

translations.literal: The army entered the pass and beheaded his general Ma Shiyao.
translations.idiomatic: The army entered the pass and beheaded his general Ma Shiyao.

sentences.zh: 尋復從南征，擊破明福王由崧，賜團龍紗衣一襲、金二千、銀二萬。

translations.literal: Soon he again followed the southern campaign, routed the Ming Prince Fu Zhu Yousong, and was granted one dragon-embroidered gauze robe, two thousand in gold, and twenty thousand in silver.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the southern campaign, defeated the Ming Prince Fu Zhu Yousong, and received one dragon-embroidered gauze robe, two thousand taels of gold, and twenty thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 嗣復從多鐸徵喀爾喀、英親王阿濟格戍大同。

translations.literal: Later he again followed Duo Duo to campaign against the Khalkha, while Prince Ying Ajige garrisoned Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Duo Duo against the Khalkha while Prince Ying Ajige held Datong.

sentences.zh: 會姜瓖叛，碩塞移師解代州圍，進親王。

translations.literal: When Jiang Xiang rebelled, Shuosai moved his army to lift the siege of Daizhou and was promoted to prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Xiang rebelled, Shuosai shifted his forces to relieve Daizhou and was promoted to prince.

sentences.zh: 諭曰：「博洛、尼堪、碩塞皆不當在貴寵之列。

translations.literal: An instruction said: 'Boluo, Nikan, and Shuosai none of them properly belong among the most highly favored.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: 'Boluo, Nikan, and Shuosai ought not to stand among the most highly favored.

sentences.zh: 茲以太祖孫故，加錫王爵。

translations.literal: Now because they are grandsons of Taizu, princely titles are additionally granted.
translations.idiomatic: Because they are Taizu's grandsons, princely titles are now granted them.

sentences.zh: 其班次、俸祿不得與和碩親王等。

translations.literal: Their precedence and stipends may not be equal to those of Princes of the First Rank.'
translations.idiomatic: Their rank and stipends may not equal those of Princes of the First Rank.'

sentences.zh: 」七年，以和碩親王下、多羅郡王上無止稱親王者，仍改郡王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because between Prince of the First Rank and Prince of the Commandery there was no title that simply read 'prince,' he was again changed to Prince of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, since no title between Prince of the First Rank and Prince of the Commandery was simply called 'prince,' he was again reduced to Prince of the Commandery.

sentences.zh: 八年，復進和碩親王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he was again promoted to Prince of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was again raised to Prince of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 迭掌兵部、宗人府。

translations.literal: He alternately headed the Ministry of War and the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as head of the Ministry of War and the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year, he died and was given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he died and received a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 第一子博果鐸，襲，改號曰莊親王。

translations.literal: His eldest son Boguoduo succeeded, and the title was changed to Prince Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Boguoduo succeeded, and the house was restyled Prince Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 雍正元年，薨，年七十四，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, he died at seventy-four; his posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Yongzheng year he died at seventy-four and was posthumously titled Jing.

sentences.zh: 無子，宗人府題請以聖祖子承襲，世宗請於皇太后，以聖祖第十六子允祿為之後，襲爵。

translations.literal: Having no son, the Imperial Clan Court memorialized that a son of Shenzu should inherit; the Shizong Emperor asked the Empress Dowager and designated Shenzu's sixteenth son Yunlu as his successor to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: Without an heir, the Imperial Clan Court proposed that a son of Shenzu inherit. The Shizong Emperor consulted the Empress Dowager and made Shenzu's sixteenth son, Yunlu, Boguoduo's successor.

sentences.zh: 居數日，上手詔謂：「外間妄議朕愛十六阿哥，令其承襲莊親王爵。

translations.literal: After several days the emperor personally issued an edict saying: 'Outsiders foolishly say that I favor the Sixteenth Prince and had him inherit the Prince Zhuang title
translations.idiomatic: A few days later the emperor issued a personal edict: 'People outside wrongly claim that I favor the Sixteenth Prince and had him inherit the Prince Zhuang title

sentences.zh: 朕封諸弟為親王，何所不可，而必藉承襲莊親王爵加厚於十六阿哥乎？

translations.literal: to enrich the Sixteenth Prince. I may enfeoff any of my younger brothers as princes of the first rank as I choose—why must I rely on inheriting the Prince Zhuang title to favor him?'
translations.idiomatic: as a special mark of favor. I may enfeoff any younger brother as a prince of the first rank as I see fit—why should I need the Prince Zhuang succession to show favor to the Sixteenth Prince?'

sentences.zh: 允祿精數學，通樂律，承聖祖指授，與修數理精蘊。

translations.literal: Yunlu mastered mathematics and understood musical theory; he received Shenzu's personal instruction and participated in compiling the Shuli Jingyun.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu was skilled in mathematics and versed in musical theory. Under Shenzu's instruction he helped compile the Shuli Jingyun.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，命總理事務，兼掌工部，食親王雙俸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong, he was ordered to oversee affairs of state, concurrently headed the Ministry of Works, and received double prince stipends.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Qianlong year he was charged with overseeing state affairs, also directed the Ministry of Works, and drew double princely stipends.

sentences.zh: 二年，？

translations.literal: In the second year, for the labor of managing affairs,
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, for exhaustion from overseeing affairs,

sentences.zh: 總理勞，加封鎮國公，允祿請以碩塞孫寧赫襲。

translations.literal: he was additionally enfeoffed as Duke Who Guards the State; Yunlu requested that Shuosai's grandson Ninghe succeed to the title.
translations.idiomatic: he was additionally enfeoffed as Duke Who Guards the State, and Yunlu asked that Shuosai's grandson Ninghe inherit that rank.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事，奪爵，仍厚分與田宅，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for an offense his title was stripped, yet he was still generously granted fields and residences; contemporary opinion praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, though stripped of the added title for an offense, he was still richly granted fields and houses, which contemporaries praised.

sentences.zh: 四年，坐與允礽子弘？

translations.literal: In the fourth year, for maintaining dealings with Hongxi, son of Yunreng,
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, for secret dealings with Hongxi, son of Yunreng,

sentences.zh: 往來詭秘，停雙俸，罷都統。

translations.literal: in secret and suspicious intercourse, his double stipend was stopped and he was dismissed as Banner General.
translations.idiomatic: his double stipend was suspended and he was removed as Banner General.

sentences.zh: 七年，命與三泰、張照管樂部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was ordered, together with San Tai and Zhang Zhao, to manage the Music Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was ordered, with San Tai and Zhang Zhao, to oversee the Music Bureau.

sentences.zh: 允祿等奏：「藉田禮畢，筵宴當奏雨暘時若、五穀豐登、家給時足三章，本為蔣廷錫所撰，樂與禮不符，不能施於燕樂。

translations.literal: Yunlu and the others memorialized: 'When the ceremonial plowing is complete, the banquet should perform the three pieces Timely Rain and Sun, Bountiful Five Grains, and Household Plenty—originally composed by Jiang Tingxi; the music does not accord with the rite and cannot be used in banquet music.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu and others memorialized: 'After the plowing rite, the banquet should play Timely Rain and Sun, Bountiful Five Grains, and Household Plenty—the three pieces Jiang Tingxi wrote—but their music does not fit the rite and cannot serve as banquet music.

sentences.zh: 請敕別撰。

translations.literal: We request an imperial order for separate composition.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that new pieces be ordered.

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「中和韶樂，例用笙四、簫笛樂之上。

translations.literal: ' They memorialized again: 'For the Harmonious and Central Serene Music, the rule calls for four sheng above the xiao and di.
translations.idiomatic: ' They memorialized again: 'In Harmonious and Central Serene Music, the rule uses four sheng above the xiao and di.

sentences.zh: 請增笙為八，簫笛為四。

translations.literal: We request that the sheng be increased to eight and the xiao and di to four.'
translations.idiomatic: We ask that the sheng be raised to eight and the xiao and di to four.'

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「漢以來各史樂志，？

translations.literal: ' They memorialized again: 'In the music treatises of every history since Han, bells and chime-stones were both counted as two,
translations.idiomatic: ' They memorialized again: 'In the music treatises of the histories since Han, bells and chime-stones were each two,

sentences.zh: 皆二，金、革二音獨出俱有鎛鐘、特磬。

translations.literal: and among the metal and hide categories alone, both the bell-chime and the special chime-stone appear separately.
translations.idiomatic: and within the metal and hide notes alone, both the bell-chime and special chime-stone appear separately.

sentences.zh: 今得西江古鎛鐘，考定黃鐘直度，上下損益，鑄鎛鐘十二。

translations.literal: Now that an ancient bell-chime from Xijiang has been obtained, the straight measure of the yellow bell has been determined, and through upper and lower augmentation and reduction, twelve bell-chimes have been cast.
translations.idiomatic: An ancient bell-chime from Xijiang has now been found; the yellow bell's straight measure has been fixed, and by raising and lowering pitch twelve bell-chimes have been cast.

sentences.zh: 竊以條理宜備始終，請仿周禮磬氏遺法，制特磬十二，與鎛鐘俱為特懸。

translations.literal: We venture that the whole system ought to be complete from beginning to end, and request that following the remnant method of the Bell-Master in the Zhou Rites, twelve special chime-stones be made and set apart with the bell-chimes as special suspended sets.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that the system should be complete from start to finish, and ask that twelve special chime-stones be made after the Bell-Master's remnant method in the Zhou Rites, set apart with the bell-chimes as special suspended instruments.

sentences.zh: 樂闋擊特磬，乃奏敔；

translations.literal: When the music ends, the special chime-stone is struck, and only then is the wooden clapper played;
translations.idiomatic: When the music ends the special chime-stone is struck, and only then is the wooden clapper played;

sentences.zh: 大祭祀、大典禮皆依應月之律，設鎛鐘、特磬各一？

translations.literal: at great sacrifices and great ceremonies, each following the pitch of the corresponding month, one set each of bell-chime and special chime-stone should be installed
translations.idiomatic: at great sacrifices and great ceremonies, following the pitch of the corresponding month, one set each of bell-chime and special chime-stone should be placed

translations.literal: in place.'
translations.idiomatic: in place.'

sentences.zh: 」上悉從之。

translations.literal: ' The emperor fully assented.
translations.idiomatic: ' The emperor approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，允祿年七十，上賜詩褒之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, when Yunlu was seventy, the emperor bestowed a poem in praise of him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, when Yunlu turned seventy, the emperor granted him a commendatory poem.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，薨，年七十三，諡曰恪。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he died at seventy-three; his posthumous title was Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he died at seventy-three and was posthumously titled Ke.

sentences.zh: 內大臣，仍管樂部、宗人府。

translations.literal: As Grand Minister of the Interior, he still managed the Music Bureau and the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Minister of the Interior and continued to oversee the Music Bureau and Imperial Clan Court.

translations.literal: His son
translations.idiomatic: His son

sentences.zh: 子弘普，輔國公，前卒。

translations.literal: Hongpu, Duke Who Assists the State, had died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Hongpu, Duke Who Assists the State, had already died.

sentences.zh: 孫永巘，襲，歷都統、領侍內大臣、御前大臣。

translations.literal: His grandson Yongyan succeeded and served as Banner General, Leading Guard Grand Minister of the Interior, and Minister Before the Throne.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yongyan succeeded and served as Banner General, Leading Guard Grand Minister of the Interior, and Minister Before the Throne.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十？

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing,
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth Jiaqing year,

sentences.zh: 五十三年，薨，諡曰慎。

translations.literal: in the fifty-third year, he died; his posthumous title was Shen.
translations.idiomatic: in the fifty-third year he died and was posthumously titled Shen.

sentences.zh: 無子，以從子綿課襲，歷都統、領侍八年，林清為亂，其徒入宮門，綿課持械拒，射傷一人，得旨議敘。

translations.literal: Having no son, his collateral nephew Mianke succeeded; he served eight years as Banner General and Leading Guard Minister. When Lin Qing raised rebellion and his followers entered the palace gates, Mianke took up arms to resist and shot and wounded one man; he received an imperial order for merit review.
translations.idiomatic: Without an heir, his collateral nephew Mianke succeeded. He served eight years as Banner General and Leading Guard Minister. When Lin Qing rebelled and his followers broke into the palace gates, Mianke armed himself to resist and wounded one man with an arrow; the court ordered his service reviewed for reward.

sentences.zh: 明年，上幸木蘭，綿課奏河橋圮於水，意在尼行，不稱上旨，坐罰俸，並罷諸職。

translations.literal: The next year, when the emperor traveled to Mulan, Mianke memorialized that a river bridge had collapsed in the water, intending to obstruct the journey—this did not accord with the emperor's intent; he was fined salary and dismissed from all his posts.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as the emperor went to Mulan, Mianke reported a river bridge washed out by water, plainly hoping to block the journey. Deemed disloyal to the imperial will, he was fined and stripped of all offices.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，坐承修裕陵隆恩殿工草率，降郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang, for negligent work on repairs to the Long'en Hall at the Yuling Mausoleum, he was demoted to Prince of the Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Daoguang year he was reduced to Prince of the Commandery for shoddy repairs to the Long'en Hall at Yuling.

sentences.zh: 四年，重修工蕆，复親王。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when the rebuilding was completed, he was restored to Prince of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, once rebuilding was finished, he was restored to Prince of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 六年，薨，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died; his posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died and was posthumously titled Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子奕鎛，嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yibo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yibo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 八年，以寶華峪地宮入水，追論綿課罪，降奕鎛郡王，並奪諸子奕貹、奕飀、奕賟、奕賡職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because the underground palace at Baohuayu flooded, Mianke's offenses were reconsidered; Yibo was demoted to Prince of the Commandery, and his sons Yizhen, Yihui, Yizhan, and Yigeng were all stripped of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, after the Baohuayu underground palace flooded, Mianke's old fault was revived: Yibo was demoted to Prince of the Commandery, and his sons Yizhen, Yihui, Yizhan, and Yigeng lost their posts.

sentences.zh: 十一年，上五十萬壽，复奕鎛親王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on the emperor's five-hundred-thousandth birthday, Yibo was again made Prince of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on the emperor's five-hundred-thousandth birthday, Yibo was again made Prince of the First Rank.

sentences.zh: 十八年九月，坐與輔國公溥喜赴尼寺食鴉片，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year, for going with Duke Who Assists the State Puxi to a nunnery to smoke opium, his title was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighteenth year he was stripped of his title for visiting a nunnery with Duke Who Assists the State Puxi to smoke opium.

sentences.zh: 上聞奕鎛浮薄無行，戍吉林；

translations.literal: When the emperor heard that Yibo was frivolous and without principle, he was exiled to Jilin;
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Yibo was frivolous and unrestrained, the emperor sent him into exile at Jilin;

sentences.zh: 又娶民女為妾，改戍黑龍江，以允祿曾孫綿護襲。

translations.literal: for also taking a commoner's daughter as concubine, his exile was changed to Heilongjiang, and Yunlu's great-grandson Mianhu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: and because he also took a commoner's daughter as concubine, his exile was moved to Heilongjiang while Yunlu's great-grandson Mianhu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 綿護，允祿次子輔國公弘曧孫，輔國將軍永蕃子也。

translations.literal: Mianhu was the son of General Who Assists the State Yongfan and the grandson of Duke Who Assists the State Hongrang, of the line of Yunlu's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Mianhu was the son of General Who Assists the State Yongfan and grandson of Duke Who Assists the State Hongrang, descended from Yunlu's second son.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，薨，諡曰勤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; posthumous title Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he died and was posthumously titled Qin.

sentences.zh: 弟綿，襲，二十五年，薨，諡曰質。

translations.literal: Younger brother Mianhua succeeded; in the twenty-fifth year he died; posthumous title Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mianhua inherited the title; in the twenty-fifth year he died and was posthumously titled Zhi.

sentences.zh: 子奕仁，襲，同治十三年，薨，諡曰厚。

translations.literal: Son Yiren succeeded; in the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he died; posthumous title Hou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yiren succeeded; in the thirteenth Tongzhi year he died and was posthumously titled Hou.

sentences.zh: 子載勳，襲。

translations.literal: Son Zai Xun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zai Xun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十六年，義和團入京師，載勳與端郡王載漪相結，設壇於其邸，縱令侵使館。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu the Boxers entered the capital; Zai Xun allied with Prince Duan Zai Yi, set up altars at his residence, and allowed them to attack the legations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth Guangxu year the Boxers entered the capital. Zai Xun joined Prince Duan Zai Yi, raised altars at his residence, and let them attack the foreign legations.

sentences.zh: 俄，授步軍統領。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed Commander of the Metropolitan Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Commander of the Metropolitan Infantry.

sentences.zh: 上奉太后幸太原，載勳從，為行在查營大臣。

translations.literal: When the emperor escorted the empress dowager to Taiyuan, Zai Xun accompanied them and served as superintendent of camp inspection at the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the empress dowager to Taiyuan, Zai Xun went with them and was named superintendent of camp inspection for the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 既，與各國議和，罪禍首，奪爵，賜自盡。

translations.literal: Later, when peace was negotiated with the foreign powers, the chief culprits were punished; he was stripped of his title and ordered to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was made with the foreign powers, the ringleaders were punished: his title was taken and he was granted suicide.

sentences.zh: 弟載功，襲。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zai Gong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zai Gong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 碩塞第二子博爾果洛，封惠郡王。

translations.literal: Shuosai's second son Bo'erguoluo was enfeoffed as Prince Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'erguoluo, Shuosai's second son, was created Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: For an offense he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his title after an offense.

sentences.zh: 世宗既以允祿襲莊親王，封博爾果洛孫球琳為貝勒，惠郡王所屬佐領皆隸焉。

translations.literal: After the Shizong Emperor had Yunlu succeed as Prince Zhuang, Bo'erguoluo's grandson Qiulin was created a beile, and all banner companies formerly under Prince Hui were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shizong Emperor had Yunlu succeed as Prince Zhuang, he created Bo'erguoluo's grandson Qiulin a beile and transferred every company that had belonged to Prince Hui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign, for an offense he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianlong reign he too was stripped of his title.

sentences.zh: 子德謹，襲輔國公。

translations.literal: Son Dejin succeeded as Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dejin inherited as Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，以奉恩將軍世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants declined in rank by degrees, inheriting as General of Imperial Grace.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended by degrees until it was held as General of Imperial Grace in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 鎮國慤厚公高塞，太宗第六子。

translations.literal: Duke of the State Gao Sai, styled Kehou, was Taizong's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sai, Duke of the State styled Kehou, was Emperor Taizong's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 初封輔國公。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，進鎮國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was promoted to Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Kangxi year he was raised to Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 高塞居盛京，讀書醫無閭山，嗜文學，彈琴賦詩，自號敬一主人。

translations.literal: Gao Sai lived in Mukden, studied on Mount Yiwulü, loved letters, played the zither and composed poetry, and styled himself Master Jingyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Sai made his home in Mukden, read on Mount Yiwulü, delighted in literature, played the zither and wrote verse, and called himself Master Jingyi.

sentences.zh: 九年，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year.

sentences.zh: 子孫遞降，至曾孫忠福，襲輔國將軍，坐事奪爵。

translations.literal: Descendants declined in rank by degrees until great-grandson Zhongfu inherited as General Who Assists the State and, for an offense, was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: The line fell by degrees until his great-grandson Zhongfu inherited as General Who Assists the State, then lost the title for an offense.

sentences.zh: 輔國公品級常舒，太宗第七子。

translations.literal: Changshu, Duke Who Assists the State at rank, was Taizong's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Changshu, holding the rank of Duke Who Assists the State, was Emperor Taizong's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 初封鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as General Who Guards the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created General Who Guards the State.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，進輔國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was promoted to Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Kangxi year he was raised to Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 十四年，坐事，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, for an offense, he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was stripped of his title for an offense.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，授輔國公品級。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was granted the rank of Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was given the rank of Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，高宗命錄太祖、太宗諸子後無爵者，授常舒子海林奉恩將軍，世襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong the Gaozong Emperor ordered the recording of descendants of Taizu and Taizong's sons who held no titles, and granted Changshu's son Hailin the rank of General of Imperial Grace in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Qianlong year the Gaozong Emperor ordered a register of Taizu and Taizong's descendants without titles and granted Changshu's son Hailin the hereditary rank of General of Imperial Grace.

sentences.zh: 再傳至慧文，卒，命停襲。

translations.literal: After two more generations Huiwen died and succession was ordered halted.
translations.idiomatic: Two generations later Huiwen died and the court ordered the line to cease inheriting.

sentences.zh: 輔國公韜塞，太宗第十子。

translations.literal: Tao Sai, Duke Who Assists the State, was Taizong's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Sai, Duke Who Assists the State, was Emperor Taizong's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 初封鎮國將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as General Who Guards the State.
translations.idiomatic: He was first created General Who Guards the State.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，進輔國公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was promoted to Duke Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Kangxi year he was raised to Duke Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-fourth year.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，授韜塞子諭德奉恩將軍，世襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong Tao Sai's son Yude was granted the rank of General of Imperial Grace in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Qianlong year Tao Sai's son Yude was granted the hereditary rank of General of Imperial Grace.

sentences.zh: 襄昭親王博穆博果爾，太宗第十一子。

translations.literal: Prince Xiangzhao Bomuboguo'er was Taizong's eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Bomuboguo'er, Prince Xiangzhao, was Emperor Taizong's eleventh son.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，封襄親王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was enfeoffed as Prince Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth Shunzhi year he was created Prince Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，薨，予諡。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died and was given a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died and received a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son, and the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 世祖八子：孝康章皇后生聖祖，孝獻皇后董鄂氏生榮親王，寧？

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor had eight sons: Empress Xiaokangzhang bore the Shenzu Emperor; Empress Xiaoxian of the Donggo clan bore Prince Rong; Consort Ning
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor had eight sons: Empress Xiaokangzhang bore the future Shenzu Emperor; Empress Xiaoxian of the Donggo clan bore Prince Rong; Consort Ning

sentences.zh: 妃董鄂氏生裕憲親王福全，庶妃巴氏生牛鈕，庶妃陳氏生恭親王常寧，庶妃唐氏生奇授，庶妃鈕氏生純靖親王隆禧，庶妃穆克圖氏生永幹。

translations.literal: of the Donggo clan bore Prince Yuxian Fu Quan; Lady Ba bore Niu'niu; Lady Chen bore Prince Gong Changning; Lady Tang bore Qishou; Lady Niu bore Prince Chunjing Longxi; Lady Muketu bore Yonggan.
translations.idiomatic: of the Donggo clan bore Prince Yuxian Fu Quan; Lady Ba bore Niu'niu; Lady Chen bore Prince Gong Changning; Lady Tang bore Qishou; Lady Niu bore Prince Chunjing Longxi; and Lady Muketu bore Yonggan.

sentences.zh: 牛鈕、奇授、永幹皆殤，無封。

translations.literal: Niu'niu, Qishou, and Yonggan all died in infancy and received no titles.
translations.idiomatic: Niu'niu, Qishou, and Yonggan all died young and were never enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 裕憲親王福全，世祖第二子。

translations.literal: Prince Yuxian Fu Quan was the Shizu Emperor's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuxian Fu Quan was the Shizu Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 幼時，世祖問志，對：「原為賢王。

translations.literal: In childhood, when the Shizu Emperor asked his ambition, he answered: 'I wish to be a worthy prince.'
translations.idiomatic: When he was still a boy the Shizu Emperor asked what he hoped to become, and he answered, 'I wish to be a worthy prince.'

sentences.zh: 」世祖異之。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor was struck by this.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor marveled at the answer.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，封，命與議政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed and ordered to join in deliberative councils.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth Kangxi year he was enfeoffed and appointed to deliberative councils.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，疏辭，允之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he memorialized to decline and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he asked to be released from those duties and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，上奉太皇太后幸五台，先行視道路，命福全扈太皇太后行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, when the emperor escorted the grand empress dowager to Wutai, Fu Quan went ahead to inspect the road and was ordered to attend the grand empress dowager on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, when the emperor took the grand empress dowager to Wutai, Fu Quan went ahead to reconnoiter the route and was ordered to escort her.

sentences.zh: 次長城嶺，上以嶺險不可陟，命福全奉太皇太后先還。

translations.literal: At Changcheng Ridge the emperor judged the pass too dangerous to climb and ordered Fu Quan to take the grand empress dowager back first.
translations.idiomatic: At Changcheng Ridge the emperor decided the pass was too steep and ordered Fu Quan to bring the grand empress dowager down first.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，太皇太后崩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the grand empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the grand empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 既繹祭，諭曰：「裕親王自太皇太后違豫，與朕同處，殊勞苦。

translations.literal: After the secondary mourning rites the emperor said: 'Since the grand empress dowager fell ill, Prince Yu has shared my burdens with exceptional toil.'
translations.idiomatic: After the secondary mourning rites the emperor said, 'Since the grand empress dowager first fell ill, Prince Yu has borne the same burdens as I have, with extraordinary labor.'

sentences.zh: 」命皇長子及大臣送王歸第。

translations.literal: He ordered the eldest imperial son and ministers to escort the prince home.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the eldest imperial son and his ministers to escort the prince back to his residence.

translations.literal: He was appointed
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed

sentences.zh: 領侍

translations.literal: Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard.

sentences.zh: 二十九年七月，噶爾丹深入烏硃穆秦，命為撫遠大將軍，皇長子允禔副之，出古北口；

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year Galdan penetrated deep into Uzhumuchin; Fu Quan was made Grand General Jingyuan, with the eldest son Yinreng as deputy, and marched out through Gubeikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twenty-ninth year, when Galdan drove deep into Uzhumuchin, Fu Quan was made Grand General Jingyuan with the eldest son Yinreng as deputy and marched out through Gubeikou.

sentences.zh: 而以恭親王常寧為安北大將軍，出喜？

translations.literal: Prince Gong Changning was made Grand General Anbei and marched out through Xifeng
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Changning was made Grand General Anbei and marched out through Xifeng

sentences.zh: 口。

translations.literal: Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Pass.

sentences.zh: 福全請發大同綠旗兵往殺虎口聽調遣，上令發大同鎮標馬兵六百、步兵一千四百從征，兼命理籓院自阿喇尼設站處量發附近蒙古兵尾大軍置驛。

translations.literal: Fu Quan requested that green-banner troops from Datong be sent to Shahu Pass to await orders; the emperor ordered six hundred cavalry and fourteen hundred infantry from the Datong garrison to join the campaign, and also instructed the Lifan Yuan to dispatch nearby Mongol troops from Arani's relay stations to follow the main army and establish posts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Quan asked that green-banner troops from Datong be sent to Shahu Pass to await orders. The emperor ordered six hundred cavalry and fourteen hundred infantry from the Datong garrison to the campaign and told the Lifan Yuan to send nearby Mongol troops from Arani's relay stations to follow the main force and set up posts.

sentences.zh: 福全又請凡諜報皆下軍中，上從之。

translations.literal: Fu Quan also asked that all intelligence reports be sent directly to the army, and the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Quan also asked that every intelligence report be forwarded to the army, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 師行，上御太和門賜敕印，出東直門送之。

translations.literal: When the army marched, the emperor personally bestowed the seal of command at the Gate of Supreme Harmony and saw them off through Dongzhimen.
translations.idiomatic: As the army set out, the emperor bestowed the seal of command at the Gate of Supreme Harmony and escorted them to Dongzhimen.

sentences.zh: 上先後遣內大臣阿密達、尚書阿喇尼、都統阿南達等出塞，命各率所部與福全師會。

translations.literal: The emperor successively sent the inner ministers Amida, Minister Arani, and Commander Aranda beyond the pass, ordering each to lead his troops to join Fu Quan's force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent inner ministers Amida, Minister Arani, and Commander Aranda beyond the pass in turn, ordering each to unite with Fu Quan's army.

sentences.zh: 上出塞，駐古魯富爾堅嘉渾噶山，命康親王杰書率師會福全，進駐博洛咎屯。

translations.literal: The emperor went beyond the pass himself, encamped at Mount Gurufuerjianjiahun, ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to lead troops to join Fu Quan, and advanced to encamp at Boluojiu Tun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor crossed the pass himself and encamped at Mount Gurufuerjianjiahun. He ordered Prince Kang Jieshu to join Fu Quan and advance to Boluojiu Tun.

sentences.zh: 又命簡親王雅布參贊福全軍事。

translations.literal: He also ordered Prince Jian Yabu to assist in Fu Quan's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Prince Jian Yabu to assist Fu Quan's command.

sentences.zh: 上先遣內大臣索額圖、都統蘇努分道出師，福全奏請令索額圖駐巴林，待師至，與會，上從之，並令蘇努同赴巴林，又趣阿密達、阿喇尼等速率兵內向分駐師所經道中以待​​。

translations.literal: The emperor had earlier sent the inner minister Sonin and Commander Sunu on separate routes; Fu Quan memorialized asking that Sonin encamp at Balin and wait for the army to arrive for a rendezvous, and the emperor agreed, also ordering Sunu to proceed to Balin and urging Amida, Arani, and the others to hurry their troops inward and garrison the routes the army would traverse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already sent inner minister Sonin and Commander Sunu by separate routes. Fu Quan asked that Sonin encamp at Balin and wait for the main force; the emperor agreed, ordered Sunu to Balin as well, and pressed Amida, Arani, and the rest to hold the roads the army would pass.

sentences.zh: 上自博洛和屯還駐舍里烏硃，遣使諭福全曰：「兵漸與敵近，斥堠宜嚴明。

translations.literal: Returning from Boluohetun the emperor encamped at Sheliwuzhu and sent messengers instructing Fu Quan: 'As our forces draw nearer the enemy, scouts must be strict and vigilant.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Boluohetun he encamped at Sheliwuzhu and sent word to Fu Quan: 'As the army drew closer to the enemy, scouting must be strict and alert.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹當先與羈縻，以待盛京及烏喇、科爾沁諸部兵至。

translations.literal: Galdan should first be held in check until troops from Mukden, Ula, Horqin, and the other banners arrive.'
translations.idiomatic: Galdan should first be restrained until the armies from Mukden, Ula, Horqin, and the other banners had come up.'

sentences.zh: 福全遣濟隆胡土克圖等以書喻噶爾丹曰：「我與汝協護黃教，汝追喀爾喀入我界，上命我等來論決此事。

translations.literal: Fu Quan sent Jelong Hutuktu and others with a letter addressing Galdan: 'You and I jointly protect the Yellow Teaching; you pursued the Khalkha into our territory, and the emperor has sent us to settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Quan sent Jelong Hutuktu and others with a letter to Galdan: 'You and I together uphold the Yellow Teaching. You pursued the Khalkha into our lands, and the emperor has sent us to judge the affair.

sentences.zh: 汝使言：'我汗遵達賴喇嘛之諭。

translations.literal: Your envoy said: My khan follows the instruction of the Dalai Lama.
translations.idiomatic: Your envoy said, 'My khan acts according to the Dalai Lama's command.

sentences.zh: '講信修禮，所關重大，今將於何地會議？

translations.literal: Good faith and ritual propriety are matters of great weight; where shall we meet to confer?'
translations.idiomatic: Good faith and proper ritual bear on weighty matters. Where shall we meet to discuss them?'

sentences.zh: 」並遺以羊百、牛二十。

translations.literal: He also sent one hundred sheep and twenty cattle.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent a gift of one hundred sheep and twenty cattle.

sentences.zh: 蘇努、阿密達師來會，福全疏言：「噶爾丹聲息漸近，臣等分大軍為三隊，三隊當置將。

translations.literal: When the armies of Sunu and Amida arrived, Fu Quan memorialized: 'Galdan's movements draw nearer by the day; we have divided the main force into three columns, and each column needs a commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Sunu's and Amida's armies arrived, Fu Quan wrote: 'Galdan's presence grows nearer daily. We have divided the main force into three columns, and each needs its own commander.

sentences.zh: 自參贊大臣以下、副都統以上在行間者，皆奮欲前驅，唯上所命。

translations.literal: From the assistant ministers down and the deputy commanders up, all in the ranks burn to advance; we await only the emperor's appointment.'
translations.idiomatic: From the assistant ministers down and the deputy commanders up, every officer in the ranks is eager to lead the charge and waits only upon the emperor's appointment.'

sentences.zh: 」上命前鋒統領邁圖、護軍統領楊岱、副都統札木素、塞赫、羅滿色、海蘭，尚書吉勒塔布、阿喇尼率前隊，都統楊文魁、副都統康喀喇、伊壘、色格印率次隊，公蘇努、彭春率兩翼，內大臣佟國維、索額圖、明珠、阿密達從王親督指揮，師遂進。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered vanguard commander Maitu, vanguard guard commander Yang Dai, deputy commanders Jamusu, Sehe, Luomanse, and Hailan, and Ministers Jiletabu and Arani to lead the van; Commander Yang Wenkui and deputy commanders Kangkala, Yilei, and Segyin the second column; Prince Sunu and Pengchun the two wings; and inner ministers Tong Guowei, Sonin, Mingzhu, and Amida to accompany the prince in direct command, and the army advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed vanguard commander Maitu, vanguard guard commander Yang Dai, deputy commanders Jamusu, Sehe, Luomanse, and Hailan, and Ministers Jiletabu and Arani to the van; Commander Yang Wenkui with deputy commanders Kangkala, Yilei, and Segyin to the second column; Prince Sunu and Pengchun to the two wings; and inner ministers Tong Guowei, Sonin, Mingzhu, and Amida to accompany the prince in direct command. The army then advanced.

sentences.zh: 八月己未朔，次烏闌布通，厄魯特兵遇。
