translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month the army halted at Ulan Butong and encountered Eleuth troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month the army reached Ulan Butong and met Eleuth forces.

sentences.zh: 黎明，整隊進，日晡，與戰，發槍？

translations.literal: At dawn they formed ranks and advanced; by late afternoon battle was joined and muskets and cannon were fired.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they formed ranks and moved forward. By late afternoon the fight was joined, and muskets and cannon opened fire.

sentences.zh: 至山下，厄魯特兵於林內隔河高岸橫臥。

translations.literal: Reaching the foothills, Eleuth troops lay across the high bank beyond the river within the forest.
translations.idiomatic: At the foot of the hills Eleuth soldiers stretched along the high far bank of the river, hidden in the trees.

sentences.zh: 師右翼阻？

translations.literal: The army's right wing was blocked by
translations.idiomatic: The army's right wing was hemmed in by

translations.literal: camels
translations.idiomatic: camels

sentences.zh: 駝以為障。

translations.literal: deployed as a barricade.
translations.idiomatic: drawn up as a living wall.

sentences.zh: 內大臣佟國綱等戰沒。

translations.literal: The inner minister Tong Guogang and others fell in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Inner minister Tong Guogang and others were killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 至昏，師左翼自山腰入，大敗之，斬馘頗河崖泥淖，夜收兵徐退。

translations.literal: By dusk the left wing entered from the mountainside and routed the enemy; many were slain at the river cliffs and in the muddy swamps, and the army withdrew slowly by night.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall the left wing broke in from the mountainside and put the enemy to rout. Many were cut down on the river cliffs and in the mire, and the army drew back slowly under cover of darkness.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上深？

translations.literal: When the report arrived the emperor rebuked him severely.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached him, the emperor rebuked him in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 諭之。

translations.literal: He issued instructions.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent down his instructions.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹遣伊拉古克三胡土克圖至軍前，請執土謝圖汗、澤卜尊丹巴畀之，福全數其罪，遣還。

translations.literal: Galdan sent the Hutuktu Yilagukesan to the army front, asking that the Tushiyetu Khan and the Jebtsundamba be handed over to him; Fu Quan enumerated his crimes and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan sent the Hutuktu Yilagukesan to the front, demanding the surrender of the Tushiyetu Khan and the Jebtsundamba. Fu Quan recited his crimes and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 越日，濟隆胡土克圖率其弟子七十人來言：「博碩克圖汗信伊拉古克三等言，入邊侵掠，大非理。

translations.literal: The next day Jelong Hutuktu came with seventy disciples and said: 'The Bogdo Khan believed Yilagukesan and the others, crossed the border to raid, which was wholly unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jelong Hutuktu arrived with seventy disciples and said, 'The Bogdo Khan listened to Yilagukesan and the rest, crossed the border, and raided, which was utterly without reason.

sentences.zh: 但欲索其仇土謝圖汗及澤卜尊丹巴，迫而致此。

translations.literal: He only sought vengeance against his enemies the Tushiyetu Khan and the Jebtsundamba and was driven to this.
translations.idiomatic: He sought only vengeance against his enemies the Tushiyetu Khan and the Jebtsundamba and was forced to this extremity.

sentences.zh: 彼今亦不敢复索土謝圖汗，原以澤卜尊丹巴予其師達賴喇嘛，榮莫大矣！

translations.literal: He no longer dares demand the Tushiyetu Khan; he would gladly give the Jebtsundamba to his teacher the Dalai Lama, which would be the greatest honor.'
translations.idiomatic: He no longer dares ask again for the Tushiyetu Khan. He is willing to give the Jebtsundamba to his teacher the Dalai Lama and calls that the highest honor.'

sentences.zh: 」福全謂之曰：「土謝圖汗、澤卜尊丹巴即有罪，唯上責之，豈能因噶爾丹之言遣還達賴喇嘛？

translations.literal: Fu Quan said to him: 'Even if the Tushiyetu Khan and the Jebtsundamba are guilty, only the emperor may judge them; how could we send the Jebtsundamba back at Galdan's word?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Quan answered, 'Even if the Tushiyetu Khan and the Jebtsundamba are guilty, judgment belongs to the emperor alone. How could we surrender the Jebtsundamba because Galdan asks?

sentences.zh: 且汝往來行說，能保噶爾丹不乘間奔逸掠我境內民人乎？

translations.literal: And as you go back and forth negotiating, can you guarantee Galdan will not seize the chance to flee and plunder our people within the border?'
translations.idiomatic: And as you shuttle back and forth with these words, can you guarantee that Galdan will not seize the moment to break away and plunder our people inside the frontier?'

sentences.zh: 」濟隆固言噶爾丹不敢妄行，福全許檄各路軍止勿擊。

translations.literal: Jelong insisted that Galdan would not act rashly, and Fu Quan agreed to order all armies along the routes to cease attacking.
translations.idiomatic: Jelong pressed his claim that Galdan would not act rashly, and Fu Quan agreed to send orders to every army on the march to hold their fire.

sentences.zh: 時盛京及烏喇、科爾沁諸軍未至，厄魯特方據險，故福全既擊敗厄魯特，欲因濟隆之請羈縻之，待諸軍至复戰。

translations.literal: At that time the armies from Mukden, Ula, and Horqin had not yet arrived; the Eleuths held strong ground; so having defeated them Fu Quan wished to detain Galdan through Jelong's request and wait for the other armies before fighting again.
translations.idiomatic: The armies from Mukden, Ula, and Horqin had not yet come up, and the Eleuths still held the high ground. Having beaten them once, Fu Quan meant to hold Galdan in check through Jelong's plea and strike again when the rest arrived.

sentences.zh: 上以福全奏下王大臣集議，僉謂福全不即進軍，明知濟隆為噶爾丹遊說以緩我師而故聽之，坐失事機，上嚴旨詰責，又以允禔與福全不協，留軍前必僨事，召先還京師。

translations.literal: The emperor submitted Fu Quan's memorial for joint deliberation by princes and ministers; all agreed that Fu Quan had not pressed the advance immediately, knowing full well that Jelong was lobbying for Galdan to delay our army yet deliberately listening; he had lost the opportunity; the emperor issued a stern decree rebuking him; because Yinreng and Fu Quan were at odds, keeping Yinreng at the front would surely ruin matters, and he was recalled to the capital first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laid Fu Quan's memorial before the princes and ministers for joint deliberation. All agreed that Fu Quan, knowing perfectly well Jelong was stalling for Galdan, had still chosen to listen and so let the moment pass. The emperor sent down a stern rebuke. Because Yinreng and Fu Quan could not work together, keeping Yinreng at the front would only wreck the campaign, and he was recalled to the capital first.

sentences.zh: 福全吳丹、護軍參領塞爾濟等偕濟隆諭噶爾丹，噶爾丹跪威靈佛前稽首設誓，復遣伊拉古？

translations.literal: Fu Quan, Wudan, the guard company adjutant Sai'erji, and others together with Jelong addressed Galdan; Galdan knelt before the Vajrabhairava Buddha, kowtowed, and swore an oath, and again sent Yilagukesan
translations.idiomatic: Fu Quan, Wudan, guard company adjutant Sai'erji, and others went with Jelong to address Galdan. Galdan knelt before the Vajrabhairava Buddha, kowtowed, and swore an oath, then again dispatched Yilagukesan

sentences.zh: 遣侍克三齎奏章及誓書詣軍前乞宥罪，出邊待命。

translations.literal: bearing a memorial and an oath document to the army front to beg forgiveness and await orders beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: with a memorial and a written oath to the front, begging pardon and pledging to wait beyond the border for the court's command.

sentences.zh: 上許之，复戒福全曰：「噶爾丹雖服罪請降，但性狡詐，我撤兵即虞背盟，仍宜為之備。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this and again admonished Fu Quan: 'Although Galdan submits and begs pardon, he is crafty by nature; once we withdraw I fear he will break faith, and you must still keep guard.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented, but warned Fu Quan again: 'Galdan may bow and beg mercy, yet he is treacherous by nature. The moment we withdraw he may break faith, and you must remain on your guard.'

sentences.zh: 」十月，福全率師還，駐哈嗎爾嶺內，疏言：「軍中糧至十月十日當盡，前遣侍郎額爾賀圖偕伊拉古克三諭噶爾丹，月餘未歸，度噶爾丹已出邊遠遁。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Fu Quan led the army back and encamped within Hamar Ridge, memorializing: 'Army provisions will be exhausted by the tenth day of the tenth month; earlier I dispatched Vice Minister E'ergitu together with Yilagukesan to address Galdan, and more than a month has passed without return; I judge that Galdan has already fled far beyond the border.'
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Fu Quan withdrew and encamped inside Hamar Ridge. He wrote: the army's grain would run out by the tenth day of the tenth month. He had earlier sent Vice Minister E'ergitu with Yilagukesan to treat with Galdan, and more than a month had passed without word. He believed Galdan had already fled deep beyond the frontier.'

sentences.zh: 」上以福全擅率師內徙，待歸時議罪，命即撤兵還京師，令福全及索額圖、明珠、費揚古、阿密達留後。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding Fu Quan guilty of unauthorized withdrawal, would settle punishment upon his return; he ordered immediate withdrawal to the capital and instructed Fu Quan, Sonin, Mingzhu, Feiyanggu, and Amida to remain behind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Fu Quan guilty of withdrawing on his own authority and reserved punishment for his return. He ordered the army to pull back to the capital at once and told Fu Quan, Sonin, Mingzhu, Feiyanggu, and Amida to stay behind.

sentences.zh: 尋奏：「噶爾丹出邊，伊拉古克三等追及於塞外。

translations.literal: Soon a memorial reported: Galdan had left the border and Yilagukesan and the others overtook him beyond the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a memorial arrived: Galdan had crossed out of the frontier, and Yilagukesan and his party overtook him beyond the pass.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹具疏謝罪。

translations.literal: Galdan submitted a detailed memorial begging pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan sent up a full memorial begging forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 」因並命福全還京師。

translations.literal: ' He also ordered Fu Quan to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: ' He also ordered Fu Quan back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，福全等至京師，命止朝陽門外聽勘，諭曰：「貝勒阿敏棄永平，代善使朝鮮，不遵旨行事，英親王以兵譟，皆取口供，今應用其例。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Fu Quan and the others reached the capital and were ordered to remain outside Chaoyang Gate pending investigation. An edict said: 'When Beile Amin abandoned Yongping, when Daishan went as envoy to Korea and failed to follow orders, when Prince Ying raised a military disturbance—all took oral testimony; that precedent should apply now.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fu Quan and his party reached the capital and were told to stay outside Chaoyang Gate for questioning. The emperor said: 'When Beile Amin abandoned Yongping, when Daishan went to Korea and defied his orders, when Prince Ying stirred up the army—all were examined by oral testimony. The same rule applies now.

sentences.zh: 」且諭允礻是曰：「裕親王乃汝伯父，倘汝供與王有異同，必置汝於法。

translations.literal: ' He also addressed Yinreng: 'Prince Yu is your uncle; if your testimony differs from the prince's, you will be punished by law.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He also warned Yinreng: 'Prince Yu is your uncle. If your account does not match his, the law will take you.'

sentences.zh: 」福全初欲錄允礻是軍中過惡上聞，聞上命，流涕曰：「我復何言！

translations.literal: ' Fu Quan had first wanted to record Yinreng's military misconduct and report it to the throne. When he heard the emperor's order, he wept and said: 'What more can I say!'
translations.idiomatic: ' Fu Quan had meant to put Yinreng's misconduct in camp on record and send it up. When he heard the emperor's order, he wept and said, 'What more is there for me to say!'

sentences.zh: 」遂引為己罪。

translations.literal: ' He then took the guilt upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: ' He then accepted the blame as his own.

sentences.zh: 王大臣議奪爵，上以擊敗厄魯特功，免奪爵，罷議政，罰俸三年，撤三佐領。

translations.literal: Princes and ministers deliberated stripping his title. Because of his merit in defeating the Eleuths, the emperor spared the title, removed him from deliberative council, fined three years' salary, and stripped three company captains.
translations.idiomatic: The princes and ministers debated stripping his rank. For his service in defeating the Eleuths, the emperor spared the title but removed him from deliberative council, withheld three years' salary, and took back three company captains.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上親征噶爾丹。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he accompanied the emperor on the personal campaign against Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the emperor on the campaign against Galdan in person.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，重修國子監文廟。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he rebuilt the Confucian temple at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he rebuilt the Confucian temple at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 封長子保泰為世子。

translations.literal: His eldest son Baotai was made heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Baotai was named heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，福全有疾，上再臨視。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year Fu Quan fell ill, and the emperor visited him twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year Fu Quan fell ill, and the emperor came to see him twice.

sentences.zh: 巡塞外，聞福全疾篤，命諸皇子還京師。

translations.literal: While touring beyond the passes, the emperor heard that Fu Quan's illness had turned grave and ordered the princes back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On tour beyond the passes, he heard Fu Quan was failing and sent the princes back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 福全薨，即日還蹕。

translations.literal: Fu Quan died, and the emperor turned back that same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Quan died, the emperor turned back the same day.

sentences.zh: 臨喪，摘纓，哭至柩前奠酒，慟不已。

translations.literal: At the mourning rites he removed his court tassels, wept before the coffin and offered wine, and could not stop grieving.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral he removed his court tassels, wept before the coffin, poured wine, and could not be comforted.

sentences.zh: 是日，太后先臨王第，上勸太后還宮，自蒼震門入居景仁宮，不理政事。

translations.literal: That day the empress dowager had already visited the prince's residence. The emperor persuaded her to return to the palace, entered Jingren Palace through Cangzhen Gate, and attended to no state business.
translations.idiomatic: That day the empress dowager had already gone to the prince's house. The emperor urged her back to the palace, entered Jingren Palace by Cangzhen Gate, and set aside all affairs of state.

translations.literal: The ministers
translations.idiomatic: The ministers

sentences.zh: 臣勸上還乾清宮，上曰：「居便殿不自朕始，乃太祖、太宗舊典也。

translations.literal: urged the emperor to return to Qianqing Palace. The emperor said: 'Lodging in a side hall did not begin with me; it is an old statute of Taizu and Taizong.'
translations.idiomatic: urged the emperor to return to Qianqing Palace. He said, 'Staying in a side hall did not begin with me. It is an old rule of Taizu and Taizong.'

sentences.zh: 」越日，再臨喪，賜內？

translations.literal: The next day he attended the mourning again and granted from the imperial stables
translations.idiomatic: The next day he went to the mourning again and granted from the imperial stables

sentences.zh: 馬二、對馬二、散馬六、駱駝十，及蟒緞、銀兩。

translations.literal: two horses, two paired horses, six spare horses, and ten camels, along with python-patterned silk and silver taels.
translations.idiomatic: two horses, two paired horses, six spare horses, ten camels, python brocade, and silver.

sentences.zh: 予諡。

translations.literal: A posthumous title was conferred.
translations.idiomatic: A posthumous name was granted.

sentences.zh: 又越日，舉殯，上奉太后臨王第慟哭，殯行，乃已。

translations.literal: Another day later the coffin was raised for burial. The emperor escorted the empress dowager to the prince's residence, where they wept bitterly; only when the procession had set out did they stop.
translations.idiomatic: Another day passed, and the coffin was borne to burial. The emperor brought the empress dowager to the prince's house, where they wept until the procession moved on.

sentences.zh: 命如鄭親王例，常祭外有加祭。

translations.literal: Orders followed the precedent of Prince Zheng: regular sacrifices plus additional sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered rites after the precedent of Prince Zheng: the usual offerings, with extra offerings besides.

sentences.zh: 御史羅佔為監造墳塋，建碑。

translations.literal: Censor Luo Zhan supervised construction of the tomb and the stele.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Luo Zhan oversaw the tomb and stele.

sentences.zh: 福全畏遠權勢，上友愛綦篤，嘗命畫工寫御容與並坐桐陰，示同老意也。

translations.literal: Fu Quan kept his distance from power, yet the emperor's brotherly affection ran deep. He once had painters render his imperial likeness seated with him in shared shade beneath a paulownia tree, showing their shared old age.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Quan shied from power, but the emperor loved him deeply. Once he had painters set his own face beside Fu Quan's under the shade of a paulownia, as a sign that they would grow old together.

sentences.zh: 有目耕園，禮接士大夫。

translations.literal: He had the Mugeng Garden and received scholar-officials with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the Mugeng Garden and received scholar-officials with proper courtesy.

sentences.zh: 子保泰、保綬。

translations.literal: His sons were Baotai and Baoshou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Baotai and Baoshou.

sentences.zh: 保泰，初封世子，襲爵。

translations.literal: Baotai, first enfeoffed as heir apparent, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Baotai, first made heir apparent, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，坐諂附廉親王允禩國喪演劇，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, convicted of toadying to Prince Lian YinSi and staging plays during national mourning, he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second Yongzheng year he was stripped of his rank for fawning on Prince Lian YinSi and putting on plays while the court was in mourning.

sentences.zh: 以保綬子廣寧襲，保綬追封悼親王。

translations.literal: Guangning, Baoshou's son, inherited; Baoshou was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Baoshou's son Guangning inherited the line, and Baoshou was posthumously made Prince Dao.

sentences.zh: 四年，諭：「廣寧治事錯繆，未除保泰朋黨之習。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict said: 'Guangning's governance is error-ridden, and he has not shaken off Baotai's factional habits.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year an edict read: 'Guangning governs badly and still keeps Baotai's factional ways.'

sentences.zh: 」奪爵，鎖禁。

translations.literal: ' His title was stripped and he was imprisoned under lock.
translations.idiomatic: ' His title was taken and he was put under lock and guard.

sentences.zh: 弟廣祿，襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guanglu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guanglu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十年，薨，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: In the fiftieth year of Qianlong he died; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fiftieth Qianlong year he died and was posthumously named Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子亮煥，襲郡王。

translations.literal: His son Lianghuan inherited as commandery prince.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lianghuan inherited as commandery prince.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十三年，薨，諡曰僖。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jiaqing he died; his posthumous title was Xi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth Jiaqing year he died and was posthumously named Xi.

sentences.zh: 孫文和，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: His grandson Wenhe inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Wenhe inherited as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were demoted by regular succession, with Prince of the State perpetually inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations declined by the usual rule until the line settled on hereditary Prince of the State.

sentences.zh: 榮親王，世祖第四子。

translations.literal: Prince Rong was the Shizu Emperor's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong was the Shizu Emperor's fourth son.

sentences.zh: 生二歲，未命名，薨。

translations.literal: At age two, before he had been named, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at two, before he had even been given a name.

sentences.zh: 追封。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed after death.

sentences.zh: 恭親王常寧，世祖第五子。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Changning was the Shizu Emperor's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Changning was the Shizu Emperor's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，封。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth Kangxi year he received his title.

sentences.zh: 十四年，分給佐領。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year company captains were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was granted company captains.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，府第災，上親臨視。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year his princely residence burned, and the emperor visited in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year fire struck his residence, and the emperor came in person.

sentences.zh: 是秋，上奉太皇太后幸五台，常寧扈從。

translations.literal: That autumn, when the emperor escorted the grand empress dowager to Wutai, Changning attended on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when the emperor took the grand empress dowager to Wutai, Changning went in attendance.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，噶爾丹深入烏硃穆秦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Galdan drove deep into Uzhumuchin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year Galdan pushed deep into Uzhumuchin.

sentences.zh: 常寧為安北大將軍，簡親王雅布、信郡王鄂扎副之，出喜？

translations.literal: Changning was made Grand General Anbei, with Prince Jian Yabu and Prince Xin Ezha as deputies, and marched out through Xifeng Pass;
translations.idiomatic: Changning was made Grand General Anbei, with Prince Jian Yabu and Prince Xin Ezha as deputies, and marched out through Xifeng Pass;

sentences.zh: 口；

translations.literal: at the same time
translations.idiomatic: at the same time

sentences.zh: 同時，裕親王福全以撫遠大將軍，出古北口。

translations.literal: Prince Yu Fu Quan served as Grand General Jingyuan and marched out through Gubei Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yu Fu Quan, as Grand General Jingyuan, marched out through Gubei Pass.

sentences.zh: 先發，旋令率師會裕親王軍。

translations.literal: He set out first, but was soon ordered to bring his army to join Prince Yu's force.
translations.idiomatic: He went out first, but was soon told to bring his army and join Prince Yu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以擊敗噶爾丹不窮追，罷議政，罰王俸三年。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, for defeating Galdan without hot pursuit, he was removed from deliberative council and fined three years' princely salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, because he beat Galdan but did not pursue him to the end, he lost his seat in deliberative council and forfeited three years' princely stipend.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，從上親征。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year he accompanied the emperor on the personal campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year he followed the emperor on campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，薨。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he died.

sentences.zh: 上方巡幸塞外，命諸皇子經理其喪，賜銀萬，內務府郎中皁保監修墳塋，立碑，遣官致祭。

translations.literal: The emperor was touring beyond the passes. He ordered the princes to manage the funeral, granted ten thousand taels of silver, had Zaobao of the Imperial Household Department supervise the tomb, erected a stele, and dispatched officials to offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still on tour beyond the passes. He put the princes in charge of the funeral, granted ten thousand taels of silver, set Zaobao of the Imperial Household Department to build the tomb, raised a stele, and sent officials to sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 上還京師，臨其喪。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital he attended the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital, he went to the funeral himself.

sentences.zh: 第三子海善，襲貝勒。

translations.literal: The third son Haishan inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: The third son, Haishan, inherited as beile.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，坐縱內監妄行，奪爵。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year, convicted of allowing eunuchs to act recklessly, he was stripped of his title.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-first year he lost his rank for letting eunuchs run wild.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年，复封。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng he was reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth Yongzheng year he was enfeoffed again.

sentences.zh: 乾隆八年，卒，諡僖敏。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qianlong he died; his posthumous title was Ximin.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth Qianlong year he died and was posthumously named Ximin.

sentences.zh: 初奪爵，以常寧第二子滿都護襲貝勒，屢坐事，降鎮國公，又以海善孫斐蘇襲貝勒。

translations.literal: When the title was first stripped, Manduhu, Changning's second son, inherited as beile; repeatedly convicted, he was demoted to Prince of the State; later Feisu, Haishan's grandson, inherited as beile.
translations.idiomatic: After the first forfeiture, Changning's second son Manduhu inherited as beile, but lost rank again and again until he fell to Prince of the State; later Haishan's grandson Feisu inherited as beile.

sentences.zh: 子孫循例遞降，以不入八分鎮國公世襲。

translations.literal: Descendants were demoted by regular succession, with Prince of the State outside the Eight Privileges perpetually inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations declined by the usual rule until the line held only hereditary Prince of the State, outside the Eight Privileges.

sentences.zh: 純靖親王隆禧，世祖第七子。

translations.literal: Prince Chunjing Longxi was the Shizu Emperor's seventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chunjing Longxi was the Shizu Emperor's seventh son.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，封。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth Kangxi year he received his title.

sentences.zh: 十四年，分給佐領。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year company captains were assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was granted company captains.

sentences.zh: 十八年七月，隆禧疾篤，上親臨視，為召醫。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighteenth year Longxi's illness grew grave; the emperor visited in person and summoned physicians.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eighteenth year Longxi's illness turned critical; the emperor came in person and sent for doctors.

sentences.zh: 是日再臨視，日加申，薨，上痛悼，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: That day he visited again. In the hour of shen Longxi died. The emperor grieved deeply and suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He visited again that same day. Longxi died in the hour of shen. The emperor mourned deeply and closed court for three days.

sentences.zh: 太皇太后欲臨其喪，上力諫乃止。

translations.literal: The grand empress dowager wished to attend the mourning; the emperor strongly remonstrated until she desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The grand empress dowager wanted to go to the funeral, but the emperor pleaded so hard that she stopped.

sentences.zh: 上复欲臨奠，太皇太后亦諭止之，留太皇太后宮中。

translations.literal: The emperor again wished to attend the offering rites; the grand empress dowager also ordered him to stop and kept him at her palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to go again to make offerings, but the grand empress dowager forbade it and kept him in her palace.

sentences.zh: 越日，上臨奠，命發帑修塋，加祭，予諡。

translations.literal: The next day he attended the offering, ordered treasury funds for the tomb, additional sacrifices, and a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he went to offer sacrifice, ordered state funds for the tomb, extra rites, and a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 子富爾祜倫，襲，明年，薨，上輟朝三日。

translations.literal: His son Fuerhulun inherited; the next year he died, and the emperor suspended court for three days.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fuerhulun succeeded; the next year he died, and the emperor again closed court for three days.

sentences.zh: 又明年，葬純親王隆禧，上臨奠。

translations.literal: The year after that, when Prince Chun Longxi was buried, the emperor attended the offering.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that, when Prince Chun Longxi was buried, the emperor came to offer sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 富爾祜倫無子，未立後，爵除。

translations.literal: Fuerhulun had no son and no heir was established; the title was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Fuerhulun left no son, no heir was chosen, and the line ended.
